SAFETY — Problem-Solution Guide

Zanzibar Safety & Health Guide

Solving: concerns about malaria, safe beaches, turtle encounters

Message us on WhatsApp with specific health concern

The Problem

Many travelers to Zanzibar face: concerns about malaria, safe beaches, turtle encounters. With 2,900 monthly searches for "zanzibar malaria" and competing narratives online, visitors need clear, evidence-based guidance from a licensed Zanzibar tour operator.

Malaria & Preventive Health

  • Risk exists: All of Zanzibar has some malaria risk, but incidence is low in tourist areas
  • Consult your doctor: Start antimalarials 1–2 weeks before travel; continue 4 weeks after
  • Common options: Atovaquone-proguanil (Malarone), Doxycycline, Mefloquine — discuss side effects with your physician
  • Dhow Coast recommendation: Bring a traveler's medical kit with prescribed antimalarials, rehydration salts, and basic first aid

Safe Swimming Beaches

  • Nungwi: Generally safe — strong currents possible at high tide; swim near resort areas with lifeguard awareness
  • Kendwa: Calm waters all day (no tide issues); full-moon party beach — swim cautiously at night
  • Paje: Lagoon swimming safe at high tide; watch for sea urchins at low tide
  • Jambiani: Safe swimming; tides expose seaweed farms — watch your step
  • Stone Town / Changuu (Prison Island): Safe with guided snorkeling; currents can be strong

Turtle Encounters & Nesting

  • Best months: July–October (nesting season), January–March (hatching)
  • Locations: Nungwi turtle sanctuary, Ras Nungwi, Kiwengwa beaches
  • Ethical guidelines: No flash photography, stay 10 meters back, never touch nesting turtles
  • Dhow Coast policy: We only offer turtle experiences with licensed guides who follow turtle conservation guidelines

Other Health Considerations

  • Sun exposure: UV index 10–12 year-round — use SPF 50+, hat, sunglasses, reapply every 2 hours
  • Dehydration: Tropical climate, active excursions — drink 3+ liters water daily
  • Food & water: Bottled water only, fruits you peel yourself, thoroughly cooked seafood
  • Insect repellent: DEET 50%+ or picaridin; apply over sunscreen (sunscreen first)
  • Prescription kit: Include antidiarrheal (ciprofloxacin or azithromycin), oral rehydration salts, bandages, antiseptic cream

Emergency Contacts & Resources

  • Ladiko Medical Centre — Stone Town: +255 24 223 5000
  • Kigoma Hospital — North Zanzibar: +255 24 265 4000
  • Emergency ambulance: 199 (Zanzibar)
  • Your travel insurance 24-hour assistance number — keep saved in phone
  • Dhow Coast Travels booking line (WhatsApp): +255 672 450 934 — available 24/7 for health referrals
